identityReview: Sanna Marin, born 16 November 1985 Helsinki; former Finnish PM 10 December 2019–20 June 2023, former transport minister and MP, now TBI Strategic Counsellor. Tampere City Council chair, not mayor. Master of Administrative Sciences in 2017, not a doctorate. Parliamentary resignation approved 12 September 2023 and effective 13 September, separate from 7 September advisory appointment announcement. Cabinet ordinal 76 is not an individual-prime-minister ordinal.
lifeStatusEvidence: St. Francis Xavier University’s 29 October 2026 account explicitly describes her completed appearance on 27 October at the Brian Mulroney Speaker Series. It reports a conversation rather than only an invitation. Current TBI directory independently confirms the advisory role.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Finnish ministerial history and original government appointment, pandemic and NATO-decree statements; European Parliament-hosted CV; Tampere alumni record; NATO accession report; Yle resignation account; current TBI biography and appointment release; publisher edition record and StFX event retrospective. Read Commons crop and parent metadata plus official FinnishGovernment Flickr source and its specific CC BY 2.0 link.
corrections: Read official Finnish historical minister record: born 16 November 1985 in Helsinki; transport and communications minister 6 June–10 December 2019; prime minister 10 December 2019–20 June 2023. Exact service dates override abbreviated accounts ending her premiership at the April election. No claim that she is current prime minister or president.

Read the short CV hosted by the European Parliament for her transport-minister period: birth, administrative-sciences master’s, MP since 2015, Tampere council chair 2013–2017 and member 2017–2021, regional council 2013–2016. Future/ongoing endpoints in this historical CV are not automatically current. Council chair is not mayor. PDF portrait has only a textual visual description; it was not visually inspected or adopted as a licensed image.

Read Tampere University alumni article confirming the 2017 Master of Administrative Sciences from the former University of Tampere and overlap with political service. It calls her the third female Finnish PM and, at appointment at 34, youngest then-serving PM worldwide; the biography uses age without turning a time-specific ranking into a permanent one. Its wording elected to city council in 2013 conflicts with commonly recorded 2012 election/2013 term start; profile only states the securely established 2013–2017 chairmanship. No invented doctorate or full-time exclusive study period.

Read 10 December 2019 actual government-appointment release: president appointed Finland’s 76th government and released Rinne ministers; 19 ministers across SDP, Centre, Greens, Left Alliance and Swedish People’s Party. The ordinal counts governments, not unique prime ministers. The biography describes coalition coordination, without treating the cabinet as one-party rule or personal power over every constitutional institution.

Read English version of government release dated 16 March 2020: joint emergency declaration, ordinary/emergency legislative framework, intended decree submission 17 March and planned school changes from 18 March, with exceptions. Final profile and all translations retain prospective wording for the decree and school start rather than claiming implementation proved solely by this advance release. Emergency declaration, submission, parliamentary oversight and measures are separate. No claim all children were barred from education, every restriction began on the 16th, or particular health/economic outcomes were demonstrated.

Read NATO’s actual 4 April 2023 accession account: instrument deposited with US government by Foreign Minister Haavisto, President Niinistö present, Finland 31st Ally; allied ratification followed July 2022 protocols. Sweden was still an invitee that day. Membership was not a unilateral act by Marin and she is not invented as the person who deposited the instrument. No quantified security benefit or fastest-ever ranking is adopted from promotional biographies.

Read Yle report of 12 September 2023, 17:28: parliament accepted resignation, effective Wednesday 13 September; she had been re-elected in April. Announcement of plans the prior week is different. Report covers criticism and support, including debate over electoral trust and socially important work. No claim of legal wrongdoing or parliamentary expulsion. Parliamentary search index lists last service day 12 September, consistent with resignation effective next day; direct parliamentary pages had no readable body.

Read current TBI expert page: Strategic Counsellor, joined September 2023, advising political leaders’ reform programmes across the institute’s portfolio. Former premiership and party leadership are distinguished from current advisory work. Promotional climate-target achievements and swiftest-NATO-accession claim are not treated as independently audited outcomes.

Read TBI press release of 7 September 2023 announcing appointment as Strategic Counsellor. This is the announcement date, distinct from parliament’s 12 September resignation approval and next-day effect. It is not an appointment to the British or Finnish government, nor evidence that every reform advised has succeeded.

Read Scribner/Simon & Schuster record for ISBN 9781668069639: English Hope in Action: A Memoir About the Courage to Lead, publisher date 4 November 2025, 256 pages. The edition and publisher date are specified rather than inferred from a forthcoming notice or applied to every translation. Read publisher description and metadata, not the whole book. Author photograph credited Elina Simonen was not adopted under an assumed open licence.

Read StFX’s 29 October 2026 report describing the completed 27 October Mulroney Speaker Series conversation at Barrick Auditorium. Discussion included uncertainty, Ukraine and women in politics. Report publication and event dates differ. Personal forecasts about war are not factual predictions or Finnish government commitments. This is recent actual-activity evidence; no original event video was watched. A future 26 November Berlin listing is not treated as attendance.

Read Finnish government release of 5 April 2023 on the domestic decree. Parliament approved the treaty on 1 March, president decided on accession 23 March; international membership took effect with deposit on 4 April. The 5 April decree completed domestic integration, not a different international accession date. National approval, allied ratification, international deposit and domestic decree are distinguished.

additionalConsulted.access: Search index lists MP/group dates 22 April 2015–12 September 2023, but direct page and parliament.fi variant had no readable lines. Full parliamentary record is not claimed as read; Yle supplies approval and effective-date distinction.

Read attribution, adaptation, commercial reuse and derivative modification obligations. Specific source licence confirmed; no claim this waives separate personality rights.
Historical separate government image-rights link failed on redirect. Its content is not represented as read.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No full memoir reading, independent assessment of pandemic outcomes or advisory-project results, original event video, complete parliamentary page rendering or portrait pixels. Historical government releases distinguish scheduled measures from confirmed implementation; current roles and event dates need refreshing before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed for 16 November 1985 Helsinki birth, 2017 administrative-sciences master’s, council chair versus mayor, overlapping study/office, 2019 ministerial dates and 20 June 2023 PM end, 19-member five-party coalition, 16 March emergency versus planned 17/18 March measures, NATO national/allied/international procedures and Sweden distinction, 7/12/13 September advisory/resignation dates, 4 November 2025 English edition, and 27 October 2026 actual StFX conversation versus 29 October report.
